findings.reason: the plan must state that every git-tag query in the copied machine is oras-backed (or that one tag-list function backs all three), because a ported `_tag_exists` that silently reads an empty git tag list lets `release` re-flag a registry tag the maps already carry.
findings.text: §18 says "one function lists the package's tags with `oras repo tags` ... and the copied state machine reads those instead", but the copied `compute_next_version` (imas_codex/cli/release.py:153) consumes three tag queries — `_get_latest_tag` (:29), `_get_latest_stable_tag` (:45) and `_tag_exists` (:87); re-pointing one leaves `_tag_exists` shelling `git tag -l`, which returns nothing on a map tree with no git history, so the RC-collision loops (:201-203, :217-219) and the abandon-RC path compute an RC tag on the assumption no tag of that name exists

findings.reason: the registry ref needs its own descriptor field (or the table needs a named file to extend), so a released bundle keeps a stable bundle name distinct from the package it is published under and the table has an owner to edit.
findings.text: §18 has `release` write the registry package name (`imas-alambic-jt60sa`) into `bundle.json`, but that descriptor's `name` is the bundle's own name (`_text(payload.get("name"), "bundle name")` at machine_map.py:174, read into `MapBundle.name` and echoed in the ambiguous-bundle diagnostic at machine_map.py:315; the committed instance is `"name": "ambix"` at imas_ambix/data/bundle.json:2), so one field would carry both the bundle's identity and the GHCR ref and the bundle's identity is lost; and §18's write paths (`imas_ambix/maps_cli.py`, `imas_ambix/cli.py`, `imas_ambix/tests/test_maps_cli.py`, `imasdb.sh`, `AGENTS.md`) name no home for the "machine-to-package table beside `paths.py`'s map directory" §18 introduces

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the proposed `imas_ambix/maps_cli.py` is one module hiding the tag-list reader, the state machine, the OCI push/pull and the tree digest behind three CLI verbs; behaviour is concentrated, not spread across shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18 makes `release` overwrite `bundle.json`'s `name` with the registry package name, a field machine_map.py already owns as the bundle's own name.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §18's "Accounting for the new surface" paragraph names what it retires (the installer's private pull path, merged into `maps pull`), states `release` and `status` have no existing command to retire, and states why the one added refusal (`pull` refusing to overwrite an unreleased local tree) has nothing that can retire it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §18 says one function lists the package's tags for the copied state machine, but `compute_next_version` (imas_codex/cli/release.py:153) consumes three git-tag queries, not one.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `maps pull` is not a bare wrapper over oras: §18 retires the installer's private `oras pull` (imasdb.sh:70) into it and says why ("so the registry, the auth form and the artifact type have one owner"), which is the extension-of-owner the item asks for.
